entities.summary: Adolfo Kaminsky was an Argentine-born member of the French Resistance, specializing in the forgery of identity documents (IDs), and a photographer. During World War II, he forged papers that saved the lives of more than 14,000 Jews. He later assisted Jewish immigration to the British Mandate for Palestine and then forged identity documents for the Algerian National Liberation Front and French draft dodgers during the Algerian War (1954–62). He forged papers for thirty years for different activist groups, mainly national liberation fronts, without ever requiring payment in order to preserve his freedom.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Adolfo Kaminsky's forgery of identity documents saved over 14,000 Jewish lives during World War II. His work continued for thirty years, assisting Jewish immigration and national liberation fronts without payment.
